newsitem.title: UK: Germany revises deficit forecast to 2.9 pct-paper.
newsitem.headline: Germany revises deficit forecast to 2.9 pct-paper.

text.p: The German government's annual economic report, due for release on Tuesday, will show an upward revision of its 1997 budget deficit forecast to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), the Financial Times reported on Monday.

The forecast was revised from the 2.5 percent expected by the Finance Ministry when it set the 1997 budget last year. But it was still just below the 3.0 percent target required to qualify for European monetary union.
The new forecast represented a sharp drop from last year's deficit of 3.9 percent of GDP.

Details of the report, obtained by Reuters last week, showed an expected rise in GDP growth to 2.5 percent this year from 1.4 percent in 1996, with a forecast drop in inflation to 1.5 percent in 1997 from 1.8 percent last year.
German unemployment was expected to rise to 11 percent from 10.3 percent last year, the report said.
